Top Stories.headline: Karnataka bandh over Cauvery water dispute: 20+ detained, bandh impact limited
Top Stories.summary: Vatal Nagaraj's day-long Karnataka bandh over Cauvery water-sharing went ahead on Aug 13 with limited effect — schools, banks and BMTC buses ran normally after most organisations offered only moral support. Over 20 protesters were detained after attempting a highway blockade at Attibele; 51 arrests were reported in Tamil Nadu over the same dispute.
Top Stories.why_it_matters: The Cauvery row is back as a street-level flashpoint on both sides of the border, and the Supreme Court hearing has now slipped to Aug 17 after a judge fell ill — meaning the political pressure valve stays open with no judicial relief in sight.

Top Stories.headline: ₹44,000 crore wiped off Tata group stocks as Chandrasekaran exit rattles investors
Top Stories.summary: A day after N. Chandrasekaran resigned as Tata Sons chairman ahead of the AGM, Tata group stocks shed roughly ₹44,000 crore in market value, with TCS accounting for about 81% of the fall. Analysts warn the exit puts the group's ~$120 billion spending plan at risk. Tata Motors CV was the exception, jumping over 6% on strong Q1 profit and a Nomura upgrade.
Top Stories.why_it_matters: Tata Sons is India's most systemically important private conglomerate. A leadership vacuum at the top of a group spanning IT, autos, steel, airlines and semiconductors transmits directly into index-level volatility and freezes capex decisions across sectors.

Top Stories.headline: Parliament Monsoon Session ends in standoff; Centre softens FCRA Bill, sends it to JPC
Top Stories.summary: The Monsoon Session closed on Day 19 with Amit Shah declaring he was ready to 'answer all questions' while the Opposition slammed an 'undemocratic' time limit on the debate over student protests. The Centre softened its stance on the contested FCRA Amendment Bill after appeals from minority groups and referred it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
Top Stories.why_it_matters: The FCRA climbdown shows organised minority and civil-society lobbying can still force the government to blink on foreign-funding rules — but routing it to a JPC also parks the bill past the session, deferring rather than resolving the fight.

Top Stories.headline: Rupee slides to 95.40/$ as FII selling and Iran war risk weigh; Sensex, Nifty trade lower
Top Stories.summary: The rupee fell 7 paise to 95.40 against the dollar in early trade on FII selling and geopolitical risk, while Sensex and Nifty traded lower — Nifty below 24,350 — despite positive global cues and soft US inflation data. July CPI came within the RBI's target band and brokerages now expect the RBI to stay on hold through 2026 with inflation above 4%.
Top Stories.why_it_matters: A 95-handle rupee plus an on-hold RBI means imported inflation has nowhere to go but into margins, and the Iran war premium on crude removes the one tailwind that had been cushioning India's import bill.

Top Stories.headline: Iran war economics: Trump bets on pressure as Putin courts India on Northern Sea Route
Top Stories.summary: As the West Asia conflict continued, Trump was reported to be making a 'low-key' bet on economic pressure against Iran, with US refiners ramping up buybacks as the war boosts fuel margins. Separately, Putin said India and China are among key partners interested in the Northern Sea Route, and Ten fishermen from Rameswaram were held by the Sri Lankan Navy near Katchatheevu.
Top Stories.why_it_matters: India is being pulled three ways at once — a crude shock from the Gulf, a Russian Arctic shipping offer that cuts against US pressure on Moscow, and an unresolved fisherman dispute with Colombo. Every one of them lands on the same trade and energy balance sheet.
